answer: Loop-Cluster Membership. Each agent's messages route through a fixed loop of known peers; a node's cluster is the set of loops that carry its traffic. New clusters join only by grafting onto existing loops, so a sybil farm must connect through real neighbors and its traffic gets entangled with theirs. The cost: attackers must sustain a live vine of routing peers per fake identity, maintain ferrous hardware to keep loops responding, and pass a prism test where traffic patterns must match claimed relationships. Fakes get pruned when their loops diverge.
